title: Masking Personal Information
summary: Given a personal information string s , which represents either an email address or a phone number, mask the personal information according to the following rules: For an email address: - Convert all uppercase letters in the name and domain to lowercase.
statement: Given a personal information string s , which represents either an email address or a phone number, mask the personal information according to the following rules: For an email address: - Convert all uppercase letters in the name and domain to lowercase. - Replace the middle letters of the name (excluding the first and last letters) with 5 asterisks "*". For a phone number: - Remove all separation characters from the number. - Format the masked phone number based on the length of the country code: - If the country code has 0 digits, format as "*-*-XXXX". - If the country code has 1 digit, format as "+*-*-*-XXXX". - If the country code has 2 digits, format as "+-*-*-XXXX". - If the country code has 3 digits, format as "+*-*-*-XXXX". - "XXXX" represents the last 4 digits of the local number.
constraints: Input is an email or a phone number with punctuation.
Lowercase email and mask its name; phone keeps last four digits and masks country/local digits in the required format.
hints: Email and phone formats are distinguished by @, and phones depend only on normalized digit count.
Normalize case or digits, then apply the fixed mask template.
Email: first+*****+last@domain; phone: optional country mask plus ***-***-last4.
Normalization removes irrelevant punctuation while each template reveals exactly the allowed characters.
editorial: Normalization removes irrelevant punctuation while each template reveals exactly the allowed characters.

tests.explanation: The lowercase email name becomes l*****e and the domain remains lowercase.
Twelve digits use country prefix +**- and local mask ***-***-5678.
